title: Rule-Based Graph Cleaning with GPUs on a Single Machine
note: Explicitly a single-machine CPU+GPU+IO pipelined system; fits the target machine by construction

title: Coach: Exploiting Temporal Patterns for All-Resource Oversubscription in Cloud Platforms
note: All-resource oversubscription policy for cloud VMs driven by Azure traces - can be replayed in a simulator; concern: no public artifact found in GitHub/web search so code availability is unclear

title: CGgraph: An Ultra-fast Graph Processing System on Modern Commodity CPU-GPU Co-processor
note: CPU-GPU cooperative graph engine that handles GPU memory oversubscription; one GPU is the target setting

title: Characterization of Large Language Model Development in the Datacenter
note: Six-month LLM development trace from a 2048-GPU datacenter is openly released (109 MB on GitHub, ~80 GB full set on Hugging Face) and supports trace-driven scheduling and failure-recovery simulation on one machine. Concerns: this is a characterization paper - the released artifact is the trace plus analysis code, not the described systems (fault-tolerant pretraining, decoupled scheduling), so an improvement project would have to be simulation-based.

title: Experimental Analysis of Large-scale Learnable Vector Storage Compression
note: modular benchmark of 14 embedding-compression methods. Concern: full recommender datasets are large, scale-down likely needed. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/HugoZHL/Hetu/tree/embedmem/tools/EmbeddingMemoryCompression .

title: Venn: Resource Management For Collaborative Learning Jobs
note: Resource manager for collaborative-learning jobs - conda-based simulator over device traces, no cluster needed - repo name Venn matches the paper even though the system is called Auxo in the text

title: LITESHIELD: Secure Containers via Lightweight, Composable Userspace μKernel Services
note: Secure containers built from composable user-space microkernel services serving most Linux syscalls in user space; the LiteShield side needs no root. Concern: baselines (Kata, KVM) need virtualization that is unavailable, so comparisons would shrink to gVisor-class user-space baselines

title: Cocktailer: Analyzing and Optimizing Dynamic Control Flow in Deep Learning
note: DNN compiler that schedules control flow into accelerator kernels; evaluated on a single GPU. CUDA toolchain installable per-user via conda. Concern: the artifact pins a specific CUDA/TVM/ROCm stack and driver 535 caps the native CUDA version at 12.2, so toolchain pinning is the main build risk. Zenodo mirror: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7856472 . Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/nnfusion/tree/cocktailer_artifact .

title: State-Aware Fuzzing of JavaScript Engines with LLM-Guided Instrumentation
note: State-aware JavaScript-engine fuzzing with LLM-guided instrumentation. Engine fuzzing is user space and CPU bound - 16 cores and 32 threads make fuzzing campaigns feasible, and coverage or bugs-per-hour is a clean testable hypothesis. Concerns: this is a testing and security tool rather than a resource-management system, no artifact public yet, and the LLM guidance costs API calls.

title: Preparation Meets Opportunity: Enhancing Data Preprocessing for ML Training With Seneca
note: Cache partitioning + opportunistic sampling in the PyTorch data loader; user-space, storage-bound, one node. Concerns: datasets in the paper range 142 GB-1.4 TB vs ~257 GB free, so a smaller dataset is needed; the paper's multi-node / NVLink configurations are out of reach, and a single A5000 limits how many concurrent training jobs can be co-run.

title: QMoE: Sub-1-Bit Compression of Trillion Parameter Models
note: Sub-1-bit MoE compression format with bespoke GPU decoding kernels for compressed inference - the decode kernel and format work on one GPU. Concern - the SwitchTransformer-c2048 headline needs 3.2 TB of weights and a 160 GB output, which does not fit the ~257 GB free disk or the download budget; only the smaller Switch base/large-128 models are realistic, so the project must be framed around the kernel/format at reduced scale.

title: Agents of Autonomy: A Systematic Study of Robotics on Modern Hardware
note: RoWild is an open-source cross-platform user-space robotics benchmark suite (C++/Python, CPU and CUDA) that the paper profiles end-to-end on everything from embedded CPUs to server GPUs; one 16-core CPU plus one A5000 covers the high-end configuration. Concern: the paper is a characterization study and its own conclusions argue for hardware changes, so an improvement project would have to target the software side (kernel fusion, batching, data structures in the motion-planning and SLAM workloads). Second concern: the published characterization leans on architectural counters that perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks, so a reproduction would be limited to wall-clock timing.

title: B-Trees Are Back: Engineering Fast and Pageable Node Layouts
note: Engineering study of pageable B-Tree node layouts with variable-size records; user-space storage engine

title: DiskJoin: Large-scale Vector Similarity Join with SSD
note: disk-based vector similarity join on a single machine with NVMe - explicit SSD access-pattern and cache-eviction design - concern: billion-scale datasets exceed the 257 GB of free disk - needs scale-down

title: Is Machine Learning Necessary for Cloud Resource Usage Forecasting?
note: Shows LSTM forecasts of cloud resource usage are effectively a one-step shift and that a trivial persistence forecast matches them, on Alibaba/Azure/Google/Bitbrains traces. Entirely CPU/GPU-optional Python notebooks on public traces - an ideal reproduce-and-extend target. Concern: it is a 11-page vision-track paper, so an improvement project must add its own downstream evaluation (e.g. autoscaling policy driven by the forecast).

title: MOST: Model-Based Compression with Outlier Storage for Time Series Data
note: Model-based time-series compression with outlier storage; CPU only

title: Sprinter: Speeding Up High-Fidelity Crawling of the Modern Web
note: Hybrid browser plus browserless web crawler with JS-execution memoization; entirely user space (Node, headless Chrome via CDP), single machine, no root. Concerns: needs a record-and-replay proxy and a page corpus; live crawling is nondeterministic and bandwidth-hungry, so the reproduction plan should pin an archived corpus. Repo has no README on main - code is on the master branch.

title: FAAQP: Fast and Accurate Approximate Query Processing based on Bitmap-augmented Sum-Product Network
note: Learned sum-product-network model used inside the DBMS for approximate query answering

title: AXE: A Task Decomposition Approach to Learned LSM Tuning
note: Decomposes learned LSM tuning into cost-model training and a separate solver so that no database executions are needed at deployment time; artifact is a self-contained Python tuner plus RocksDB harness

title: TQEx: Tensor-based Query Engine Enhanced by Bridging the Gap
note: relational query engine compiled onto tensor-computation runtimes - an ML-compiler/runtime style artifact runnable on one GPU - concern: paper targets several XPU backends - no repo located

title: Q-Hitter: A Better Token Oracle for Efficient LLM Inference via Sparse-Quantized KV Cache
note: Joint KV-cache sparsification + quantization (quantization-friendly heavy hitters); repo link is in the paper. Single-GPU, 7B-class models. Concern - much of the released code is accuracy-side; end-to-end throughput/memory gains may need to be wired into a serving engine by the team.

title: Flexible Non-intrusive Dynamic Instrumentation for WebAssembly
note: Non-intrusive bytecode-level dynamic instrumentation in the Wizard WebAssembly research engine; user-space, CPU-only, written in Virgil.

title: MinatoLoader: Accelerating Machine Learning Training Through Efficient Data Preprocessing
note: General-purpose PyTorch data loader that removes preprocessing stalls - single GPU plus 16 CPU cores is exactly the setting, artifact available. Very strong fit

title: ExoFlow: A Universal Workflow System for Exactly-Once DAGs
note: User-space workflow runtime built on Ray; the contribution (decoupling recovery from execution via task annotations and references) is a runtime design that Ray can exercise with multiple processes on one host. Concern: the paper's evaluation uses AWS clusters and serverless backends, so the team would need to scale the workloads down to a local Ray cluster.

title: Logical and Physical Optimizations for SQL Query Execution over Large Language Models
note: Logical and physical operators and optimizations for executing queries over LLMs; concern - relies on LLM API calls

title: Reqo: A Comprehensive Learning-Based Cost Model for Robust and Explainable Query Optimization
note: learning-based, uncertainty-aware and explainable cost model for query optimization - learned component inside PostgreSQL - GNN training fits one GPU

title: CacheMind: From Miss Rates to Why – Natural-Language, Trace-Grounded Reasoning for Cache Replacement
note: LLM plus RAG reasoning over cache traces with a released benchmark; trace-driven and CPU-only. Concern: the repo is author-named and not linked from the paper so ownership is unconfirmed

title: Icarus: Trustworthy Just-In-Time Compilers with Symbolic Meta-Execution
note: DSL plus symbolic meta-execution engine for JIT compiler transformations; entirely user-space, no root, no special hardware. Companion repo https://github.com/PLSysSec/icarus-firefox integrates with SpiderMonkey. Metric (symbolic-execution time, transformations covered) supports a testable improvement hypothesis. Concern: PL/verification rather than a systems resource-management artifact, and building Firefox from source is a heavy 10-week-budget item.

title: An Efficient Transfer Learning Based Configuration Adviser for Database Tuning
note: transfer-learning knob adviser for DBMS tuning; PostgreSQL/MySQL run in user space

title: Pylo: Towards Accessible Learned Optimizers in PyTorch
note: CUDA-accelerated learned-optimizer kernels exposed through torch.optim; the reported throughput gains are single-GPU ViT-B/16 training numbers. Concern: the large-scale pre-training claims assume more compute than one A5000

title: Grep: A Graph Learning Based Database Partitioning System
note: Graph-learning model that picks partitioning keys - a learned component replacing a DBA heuristic. Concern: target is a distributed DBMS so end-to-end gains need multiple nodes; the learning part alone is single-node. No repo found

title: Finding Adversarial Inputs for Heuristics using Multi-level Optimization
note: Tool that encodes a heuristic and its optimal counterpart for a solver to find worst-case performance gaps; runs entirely in user space on CPU. Concerns: needs Gurobi (free academic license) and the .NET/C# toolchain, neither preinstalled but both installable in $HOME; the contribution is an optimization/encoding framework, so an improvement would be algorithmic rather than systems-performance.

title: Unlocking True Elasticity for the Cloud-Native Era with Dandelion
note: User-space Rust serverless worker node; the headline claim (sandboxes that cold-start in 100s of microseconds, 96% less committed memory on the Azure Functions trace) is a single-machine, trace-driven result. Concerns - the kvm isolation backend is unusable (no /dev/kvm) and the Firecracker baseline needs KVM, so only the mmu process-isolation backend is reproducible; the mmu worker README asks for an exec-mounted /dev/shm which normally needs root and would need a workaround.

title: Mimesys: Generating Realistic Executable Testing Environments from Resource Usage Traces
note: Synthesises executable contention workloads from resource-usage traces; artifact runs on plain Linux, the diffusion model trains on one GPU, and cgroup v2 cpu/memory delegation supports the contention experiments. Concern: fidelity claims involve memory-bandwidth contention, which is hard to *measure* here without hardware counters

title: Pie: A Programmable Serving System for Emerging LLM Applications
note: Decomposes the generation loop into handlers driven by user WebAssembly "inferlets"; all sandboxing is user space and the evaluation model sizes fit one 24 GB GPU. Strong candidate for an improvement project (new KV-cache strategies are the paper's own stated extension point). Concerns - none major; needs a Rust toolchain installed in user space.

title: Updatable Learned Indexes Meet Disk-Resident DBMS - From Evaluations to Design Choices
note: Systematic disk-resident evaluation of updatable learned indexes vs B+-tree with released code - ideal reproduction-or-improvement target on NVMe

title: AeonG: An Efficient Built-in Temporal Support in Graph Databases
note: built-in temporal storage support in a graph database; JVM installable through conda

title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
note: KV-cache offloading to CPU memory with speculative prefetch - designed exactly for one GPU plus large host DRAM. 125 GiB RAM and 24 GB GPU are a good match and no root is needed

title: Modyn: Data-Centric Machine Learning Pipeline Orchestration
note: Open-source orchestration platform for continuous ML training pipelines; runs on one node

title: Operation-Aware Hybrid Locking for Modern In-Memory Indexes
note: Operation-aware hybrid lock that picks optimistic version locking batching or MCS per operation type inside in-memory indexes; a concurrency-library contribution that suits a 32-thread machine

title: High Throughput and Low Latency LLM Serving via Adaptive KV Caching
note: Adaptive partial-token KV caching with parallel recomputation and GPU-CPU offload - the central memory-versus-recompute trade-off is a single-GPU question. No code found yet

title: MAGPY: Compiling Eager Mode DNN Programs by Monitoring Execution States
note: Guard and graph-capture design for eager-mode PyTorch programs - a pure user-space compiler/runtime that needs one GPU at most, with graph-completeness and speedup as crisp metrics to beat against TorchDynamo

title: Spruce: a Fast yet Space-saving Structure for Dynamic Graph Storage
note: Space-efficient in-memory dynamic graph storage structure; 125 GiB RAM is ample

title: Accelerating String-Heavy Queries with LLM Token Tables
note: Reuses an LLM tokenizer as a global string symbol table so joins and aggregations run on encoded data. Concern: implemented inside Umbra which is not open source although the authors released a token-table artifact repo

title: Interference-aware Edge Runtime Prediction with Conformal Matrix Completion
note: Learned interference-aware runtime prediction (conformal matrix completion) - training and evaluation are offline on the released WebAssembly runtime dataset (also on Zenodo record 14977004) so no edge fleet is needed to reproduce the model

title: ELECT: Enabling Erasure Coding Tiering for LSM-tree-based Storage
note: Hybrid replication/erasure-coding tiering for an LSM-tree KV store, implemented on Cassandra. Borderline on the machine: the artifact appendix recommends at least eight networked machines (six for the EC stripe). Co-locating 6-8 Cassandra JVMs as processes on this single host is possible within 125 GiB and is the standard CCM-style setup, and the headline storage-savings claim is not latency-sensitive; end-to-end throughput/latency numbers would not transfer. Needs Java in user space (not installed, but conda-installable) and Intel ISA-L, which builds from source. Audit stage should judge whether the single-host scale-down is acceptable.

title: Accelerating Graph Indexing for ANNS on Modern CPUs
note: SIMD and memory-access optimizations for HNSW-style graph index construction on modern CPUs

title: Intra-Query Runtime Elasticity for Cloud-Native Data Analysis
note: Runtime elasticity - changing degree of parallelism mid-query; concern - built on Presto, which is normally run distributed

title: A Spark Optimizer for Adaptive, Fine-Grained Parameter Tuning
note: multi-objective ML tuning of Spark adaptive-query-execution parameters; Spark runs local or pseudo-distributed

title: CoDec: Prefix-Shared Decoding Kernel for LLMs
note: shared-prefix attention kernel for the decode stage with workload balancing - a CUDA kernel compared against FlashDecoding - runs on one Ampere GPU (no FP8 needed)

title: Virtuoso: Enabling Fast and Accurate Virtual Memory Research via an Imitation-based Operating System Simulation Methodology
note: User-space simulation methodology for virtual-memory research - runs entirely on CPU, no root, and is explicitly built as a research platform to extend

title: Privacy and Accuracy-Aware AI/ML Model Deduplication
note: Deduplication of model weights for serving systems; user-space, single GPU; concern - part of the contribution is privacy analysis

title: Ave: Guiding Agentic GPU Optimization Using Data-Flow Invariants
note: ARGUS - agentic generation of GPU kernels guided by compile-time data-flow invariants, with a tile-based Python DSL. Kernel generation and benchmarking work on a single GPU. Concerns: the DSL exposes modern tensor-core or TMA style instructions that may assume Hopper rather than Ampere sm_86, and reproducing the agent loop costs LLM API calls. No artifact URL in the preprint.

title: VIDUR: A LARGE-SCALE SIMULATION FRAMEWORK FOR LLM INFERENCE
note: LLM-inference simulator + benchmark suite: schedulers, batching policies and parallelism can be studied without a cluster, which is ideal for a one-machine project. Released profiling data avoids needing the original hardware. Concern - validating the simulator against real runs on an A5000 requires re-profiling operators locally; multi-GPU configurations remain simulation-only.

title: From Learning to Recycling: A Log-Structured Learned-Less Index
note: learned index built by merging linear models, integrated into LSM-tree compaction - learned component inside a storage engine - concern: no repo located

title: SG-Serve: Efficient Model Serving for Subgraph-based Graph Representation Learning
note: serving system for subgraph-based GNNs with CPU work-stealing extraction and workload-aware GPU batching - scheduling plus model serving on one machine - concern: no repo located

title: HotPrefix: Hotness-Aware KV Cache Scheduling for Efficient Prefix Sharing in LLM Inference Systems
note: hotness-aware KV-cache scheduling for prefix sharing in LLM serving - core mechanism is a cache/scheduling policy - concern: no abstract or repo found yet - serving scale may need scale-down to a 7-8B model on 24 GB

title: MorphingDB: A Task-Centric AI-Native DBMS for Model Management and Inference
note: PostgreSQL extension with LibTorch for model storage, selection and batched inference - in-DB ML runtime that fits one GPU

title: Automated Algorithm Design for Auto-Tuning Optimizers
note: LLM-synthesized optimization algorithms for auto-tuning search spaces; BLADE plus Kernel Tuner run entirely in user space and the tuning targets include ordinary CUDA kernels. Concerns: the paper sweeps six hardware platforms - only one GPU is available here - and generation requires LLM API budget

title: ForestTI: A Scalable Inverted-Index-Oriented Timeseries Management System with Flexible Memory Efficiency
note: In-memory inverted-index structures for time-series ingestion with a tunable memory/throughput knob - storage engine work on one node. Concern: no artifact found

title: Data Caching for Enterprise-Grade Petabyte-Scale OLAP
note: Local SSD cache for petabyte-scale OLAP - admission, eviction, quota and page-affinity policies are exactly the caching topic and can be studied trace-driven on one NVMe disk. Concern: the paper is a deployed-systems experience report with no dedicated artifact; the implementation it describes is the local cache inside Alluxio open source, so the mapping from paper to code has to be verified

title: RadixGraph: A Fast, Space-Optimized Data Structure for Dynamic Graph Storage
note: radix-tree vertex index plus snapshot-log edge storage for dynamic graphs - a storage data structure with an open artifact - concern: graph-specific rather than general-purpose storage

title: ADOPT: Adaptively Optimizing Attribute Orders for Worst-Case Optimal Join Algorithms via Reinforcement Learning
note: RL-based adaptive attribute ordering for worst-case optimal joins; Java/C++ single node

title: SpInfer: Leveraging Low-Level Sparsity for Efficient Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
note: Sparse LLM inference with a bitmap sparse format and SpMM kernel, evaluated on a single GPU with Tensor Cores. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - kernels are tuned for A100 and RTX 4090; they should compile for SM86 but performance tuning constants likely need revisiting, which is itself a plausible improvement angle

title: Decentralized Actor Scheduling and Reference-based Storage in Xorbits: a Native Scalable Data Science Engine
note: Decentralized actor scheduling and reference-based intermediate storage for data-science pipelines. Concern: designed for a cluster but runs as multiple processes on one host

title: Efficient GPU Kernels for N:M-Sparse Weights in Deep Learning
note: GPU SpMV and SpMM kernels for general N to M sparse weights - pure single-GPU kernel work in the nmsparse_artifact branch of SparTA - concern - evaluated on A100 and the artifact uses Docker so it needs a user-space rebuild and retuning for Ampere consumer cards. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/microsoft/SparTA/tree/nmsparse_artifact .

title: Adjusted Objects: An Efficient and Principled Approach to Scalable Programming
note: Pure user-space Java concurrency library (DEGO) of "adjusted" shared objects, exactly the "runtimes / concurrency libraries" case in the topic table. Evaluated on a single server-class multicore with JMH-style microbenchmarks plus a Retwis-like workload; 16c/32t and 125 GiB RAM are adequate. JDK installs in user space via conda. No GPU, no root, no kernel features needed. Concern: original numbers come from a machine with more hardware threads, so absolute scalability curves will differ.

title: DecDEC: A Systems Approach to Advancing Low-Bit LLM Quantization
note: Best machine fit in the venue: the paper's own evaluation uses a single consumer GPU (RTX 4050 Mobile, RTX 4090) with CPU-side residual storage over PCIe, and targets 3-4 bit Llama-3-8B-class models that fit 24 GB comfortably. Concerns: repo does not appear in the OSDI AE results list, so artifact quality is unverified; kernels may assume Ada-class PCIe/GPU behaviour and need checking on Ampere.

title: Triton-Sanitizer: A Fast and Device-Agnostic Memory Sanitizer for Triton with Rich Diagnostic Context
note: Device-agnostic memory sanitizer for Triton kernels; user-space, single GPU. Concern: the AE scripts assume a ROCm Docker image so the NVIDIA path needs porting since Docker is unavailable

title: DobLIX: A Dual-Objective Learned Index for Log-Structured Merge Trees
note: Learned index co-optimized with LSM data access plus an RL agent that tunes parameters, integrated into RocksDB

title: Is Your Learned Query Optimizer Behaving As You Expect? A Machine Learning Perspective
note: critical re-evaluation of learned query optimizers; released harness makes a careful reproduction straightforward

title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
note: CPU-GPU-IO pipelined MoE offloading evaluated on a single 16 GB T4 - directly reproducible on one 24 GB A5000. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/caoshiyi/artifacts/tree/asplos25 .

title: RWalks: Random Walks as Attribute Diffusers for Filtered Vector Search
note: Index-agnostic filtered vector search; single machine, CPU

title: Saving Private Hash Join
note: Larger-than-memory hash join with a unified buffer pool and memory allocation across concurrent joins, implemented in DuckDB; single node

title: AnyBlox: A Framework for Self-Decoding Datasets
note: WebAssembly self-decoding dataset format integrated with DuckDB and Spark; Rust and wasm toolchains install in user space

title: Exploiting Hardware Utilization and Adaptive Dataflow for Efficient Sparse Convolution in 3D Point Clouds
note: Sparse-convolution engine for 3D point clouds with a coded-CSR format and adaptive dataflow - single-GPU kernel work with released code - concern - point-cloud datasets such as SemanticKITTI are large and the CUDA code targets older toolkits

title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
note: Scheduling-based determinism for LLM inference using verified speculation instead of batch-invariant kernels. Runs on one GPU with a 7-8B model. Official Microsoft repo referenced from the preprint. One of the strongest candidates on this list for a 10-week improvement project.

title: Concurrent Path-Copying Update to Tree Structures
note: library providing concurrent path-copying snapshots for tree structures - a user-space concurrency library - concern: no repo located

title: Breaking the Ice: Analyzing Cold Start Latency in vLLM
note: Near-ideal fit: characterizes vLLM cold-start as a predominantly CPU-bound six-step process on one GPU, ships benchmark scripts and an analytical model. Improvement axis (cutting startup latency, better prediction) is directly testable on the A5000

title: Pecan: Cost-Efficient ML Data Preprocessing with Automatic Transformation Ordering and Hybrid Placement
note: Input-pipeline preprocessing: the transformation-reordering half is a single-node tf.data question and directly testable here. Concern: the placement half assumes disaggregated remote CPU workers and the original evaluation runs on cloud VMs/TPUs, so the hybrid-placement results cannot be reproduced
